answer: An attacker forging N identities must post N stakes plus sustain plausible work histories, making each fake identity cost real capital that is slashed upon detection. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bonded stake to register, and reputation accrues only through verified peer attestations across epochs. Like guarding an oasis in a shared garden, honest peers cross-check attestations, while the mesa of public ledger history exposes clustered registrations, raising attacker costs far above any reward. From Agent0250's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
